output.review_comment:
The overall direction (preserve mixed-case tokens, capitalize first/last words, and treat the word after a colon as the start of a new "subtitle") is reasonable, but a few things concern me enough to hold off on merging:

1. **The PR description reads like it was reverse-engineered from the failing test cases rather than from a documented spec.** It calls out very specific literal examples ("iPhone and NASA", "for" at the end, "field: a year") that look copied straight from the test file rather than derived from a general rule description. That's a warning sign that the fix may only be broad enough to make the *given* assertions pass, not necessarily correct for the full editorial spec.

2. **The colon/subtitle handling looks asymmetric and likely incomplete.** The code capitalizes the small word immediately *after* a colon (treating it as the start of a subtitle) but does nothing special for the small word immediately *before* a colon. Most title-case style guides (and the "capitalize first/last word" framing used elsewhere in this same diff) also require capitalizing the last word of each subtitle segment, not just the first word of the next one. As written, `"a guide to: the end of"` would presumably leave "to" lowercase even though it's the last word before the colon. If the real spec calls for symmetric treatment, this will silently misbehave outside the specific cases the current tests cover.

3. **The mixed-case/acronym heuristic (`any(c.isupper() for c in word[1:])`) is a blunt instrument.** It will preserve *any* word with an uppercase letter after position 0 — including something like "McDonald'S" typos or emphatic ALL-CAPS words that aren't meant to be acronyms — and it takes priority over the small-word rule, so an all-caps small word (e.g. "OF") would be preserved verbatim instead of following title-case rules. This might be exactly what the editorial spec wants, but it's not obviously documented anywhere in the code, only inferred from the test cases the agent looked at.

Since the teammate explicitly said the tests encode the agreed spec and shouldn't change, the fix needs to be judged not just on "does it turn the suite green" but on whether it implements a coherent, generalizable rule set. I'd like the author to either point to (or add) a short comment/docstring describing the actual rules being encoded (especially the subtitle-boundary and acronym-preservation rules), and confirm the last-word-before-colon case is intentionally out of scope rather than an oversight, before this is merged.
